docs.title: OpenTracker (syamajala fork)
docs.text:
OpenTracker is an open-source, clean-room firmware for the original Polyend Tracker, written from behavioural specifications. It contains no Polyend code, fonts, icons or graphics, and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Polyend.

This fork follows upstream OpenTracker's 3.x line (currently 3.0.0) and adds features on top. Projects stay compatible: the fork's additions are stored in extra files next to project.mt, so stock firmware, upstream OpenTracker and the Tracker Mini still open them.

These are the docs for main

The site shows the documentation of the development branch. Once the fork makes releases, a version picker at the top selects the docs that match your image.

docs.title: What this fork adds
docs.text: Feature In short Card synths and effects Eleven extra synths (DX7, FM4, JU6, the Types) and six master effects, loaded from the SD card's Modules/ folder. Master effects The FX bank (Shift + Master): Dirt, LoFi, Chorus, BBD chorus, Echo and Tape on the whole mix. Track timing Speed (1/8x to 2x) and Groove (swing, shuffle, laid back) per track and per pattern. DX7 synth A 6-operator FM engine that plays Yamaha DX7 voices from .syx banks. Live resampling Record the master, one track or Line in while the pattern keeps playing; slice the take and place it on a track. Performance mode 16 scenes with a crossfader, fader ranges that stage a fade column by column, scene banks you can export and import, master FX (DJ filter, tape stop) and MIDI CC columns that play an external synth. Song mode Repeat counts, a Performance scene per song slot, and fader ramps between scenes. Multisample instruments Load an .sfz as one instrument that plays the nearest sampled note across the keys. USB audio The Tracker as a USB sound card: play and sample the computer's audio, record the Tracker on the computer. MIDI instrument LFO A tempo-locked LFO per MIDI instrument: CC, pitch bend or pressure. MIDI presets Save a synth's MIDI setup (CC slots with names, LFO) and load it into any MIDI instrument; presets for several synths included. More Instrument library, Memory page, slices to pattern, chord entry, piano pads and chord hints, note names, plus a summary of the 2.x features from upstream. Remote control Drive a Tracker from a computer: scripts, screen text, a live mirror.

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text:
• Installing the firmware and the card modules, and getting back to stock firmware: Install and go back.
  • Something went wrong: Troubleshooting.
  • Building, testing or contributing: the Developers section.

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• The synth engines are our own design: their settings follow the Tracker Mini, and the sound is close but not identical.
  • Wavetable and granular samples play the left channel only.
  • Synth notes take the Performance filters, panning and sends; bit depth, overdrive, the LFOs, start / end and direction act on samples only (#30). The master FX include synth notes.
  • The synth voice pool defaults to 4 voices because of the processor's speed.
  • USB audio works with Linux and Windows computers, not macOS.
  • USB Storage mode: back up the card before first use.
  • The USB ID is the pid.codes test ID 1209:0001.

Screenshots in these docs come from the desktop simulator, which runs the same code as the firmware.

docs.title: Get an image
docs.text:
The firmware image is a single file named like PolyendTrackerOTv300.ptf (for version 3.0.0). Three ways to get one:

  • Releases: tagged versions are published on the fork's Releases page, with Modules.zip (the card modules, below) and MidiPresets.zip.
  • CI builds: every push to main builds an image. Open the latest CI run on main and download the firmware-… artifact (you need to be logged in to GitHub).
  • Build it yourself: see Building.

Keep the file name

The Tracker's update bootloader only accepts names of exactly 24 characters. Don't rename the .ptf file.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
1. Copy the .ptf file to the /Firmware folder on the Tracker's SD card (or use USB Storage mode to copy it without taking the card out).
  2. On the Tracker, go to Config > Firmware update, select the file and confirm.
  3. If the screen stays dark after the update, press the power button once.

docs.title: Install the modules
docs.text:
DX7, the other extra synths and the master effects aren't in the firmware image: they are card modules, .otm files the Tracker loads from the SD card. The five Mini synths (ACD, FAT, VAP, WTFM, PERC) are built in and need nothing.

  1. Download Modules.zip from the same release as the firmware.
  2. Unzip it. It holds two folders: Modules, with the .otm files, and Help, with the help texts of Edit Patch and of Config.
  3. Copy both folders to the top of the SD card, so the files sit in /Modules/ (for example /Modules/dx7.otm) and /Help/. If the folders are already there, replace all of their files.
  4. Restart the Tracker.

What's in it:

Kind Modules Synths dx7 (DX7), fm4 (FM4), ju6 (JU6), dtype (D-Type), cstype (CS-Type), atype (A-Type), ttype (T-Type drums), eight (8-Type), hand (Hand-Type), btype (B-Type), arc (Arc-Type) Effects dirt, lofi, chorus, bbd, echo, tape
  • The card synths show in a synth slot's Model list, and the effects in the FX bank. A module only takes memory while a project uses it; Config > Memory shows what is loaded.
  • You can leave out modules you don't want: delete their files from /Modules/.
  • Update the modules with every firmware update. Modules from another firmware version don't load: the boot screen says the module "needs updating".
  • In USB Storage mode you can copy synth modules without a restart: leaving USB Storage mode reads /Modules/ again. A changed effect module needs a restart.
  • Without the folder the Tracker works as before, without those synths and effects. A project that uses a missing synth opens with "Synth N (name) not available" on that slot.

docs.title: Go back to stock firmware
docs.text:
Keep Polyend's stock image, PolyendTracker_1.9.2.ptf, in /Firmware too. Then either:

  • install it the same way, from Config > Firmware update, or
  • if OpenTracker doesn't start: put the stock file's name in a text file /Firmware/ot_restore.txt and power-cycle the Tracker. This check runs before anything else in OpenTracker, so it works even when the rest of the firmware doesn't.

Keep /Firmware tidy

The rear reset button installs a random .ptf from /Firmware. Keep only the image you want plus the stock one there.

docs.title: Projects
docs.text:
• Projects are saved in the Tracker Mini 2.2.1 format (16-track patterns, three synth slots). Older original-Tracker projects open as they are, with tracks 13–16 empty.
  • The fork's additions (Performance scenes, song counts and scenes, MIDI LFOs) are stored in extra files next to project.mt. Stock firmware, upstream OpenTracker and the Tracker Mini ignore them and open the project normally.
  • Stock firmware for the original Tracker reads only tracks 1–8 of 2.x projects (expected from the stock loader's rules; not yet confirmed on a stock unit).

docs.title: Firmware
docs.text: Needs the Arm GNU toolchain (arm-none-eabi-gcc; CI uses 14.2.Rel1, use the same one: a newer gcc builds a few KB bigger, so the flash gate disagrees with CI), Python 3 with pyelftools (tools/make_otm.py, the card modules) and the two module repositories: the synth engines (opentracker-synths) and the effects (opentracker-fx), side by side. These are the fork's copies of upstream's (opentracker-fw), kept in step with it; CI builds with them, so a fork module change (e.g. the Performance FX rows,

docs.title: 159) is in.
docs.text:
The Makefile picks up Arm's toolchain by itself from /Applications/ArmGNUToolchain/ (macOS) or ~/opt/arm-gnu-toolchain-*-arm-none-eabi/ (Linux: unpack arm-gnu-toolchain-14.2.rel1-x86_64-arm-none-eabi.tar.xz from Arm's downloads there); otherwise it uses arm-none-eabi- on the PATH, or CROSS=/path/to/arm-none-eabi-. Run make clean after switching compilers.

git clone https://github.com/syamajala/opentracker-synths
git clone https://github.com/syamajala/opentracker-fx
make clean
make -j MODULES_DIR=$PWD/../opentracker-synths

MODULES_DIR defaults to ../../opentracker-synths (two levels up, where CI puts it); set it, or export it once, if the repositories sit next to this one. opentracker-fx is found next to opentracker-synths.

A build profile (profiles/<name>.toml, PROFILE=, default full) picks the modules compiled into the image: full has ACD, FAT, VAP, PERC and WTFM; core has none. Each profile builds into build/<profile>/.

Card modules (fork #21): a profile entry with card = true stays out of the image. make card builds it as build/<profile>/otm/<name>.otm for the card's Modules/ folder, and the host builds (make host-test, the simulator, the tools) compile it in, as a device with the card's modules would have it. in_tree = true takes the module's path from this repository instead of MODULES_DIR. full builds in the five Mini synths (ACD, FAT, VAP, PERC, WTFM); its other synths are card modules: DX7 (modules/dx7 in opentracker-synths), FM4S, JU6S, D-Type, CS-Type, A-Type, T-Type, 8-Type, Hand, B-Type and ARC, and every master effect of opentracker-fx (Dirt, LoFi, Chorus, BBD, Echo, Tape). No image has those built in.

At boot the firmware looks at every Modules/*.otm (src/core/modules/module_files.h): a synth module is only listed, so its engines show in the Model list; a master effect (a master insert or a settings page) is only listed too, for the FX bank; any other module (slot effects only) loads into the card pool for good. The card synths in the pool are the ones the project's synth slots and synth presets (P1-P8) use: Open loads them once the presets are read, before the slots' patches, and a Model change loads the new one once the choice has rested for 1/4 s, while stopped (while playing the slot says "Loads at Stop"). Every load starts the synth voices over (SynthBank::holdEngines), and the slots' synths share the fast block again. A synth that doesn't fit the pool (all the room the 25 KB stack floor leaves, about 45 KB on full, at most 64 KB for the 16-bit cuts) stays unloaded, with "Card memory full" on its slot; the slots get the room first, then the presets. Two slots on one engine load it once.

Card master effects load with the card synths, in the same load set (App::syncCardSynths, src/core/app/master_fx.cpp): the ones that are on, the ones Turn on asked for (at once while stopped, else at the next Stop) and, at Open, the ones the project's sidecar has a chunk for (those that are off leave again). An effect that is turned off leaves at the next Stop. While an effect is out, its project data waits in the sidecar's kept chunks (App::stashModuleSection), so it is saved with the project and comes back when it loads. Its SDRAM (ModuleInfo::sdramBytes: Echo's 48 KB line) comes from the top of the sample memory (SampleBank::setModuleHold, after the samples; ModuleHost::setCardSdram hands it to its attach()). The master chain runs in a fixed order by module id (ModuleHost::chainOrder), the same built in or from the card, and holds up to 8 inserts.

Leaving USB storage mode lists Modules/ again (rescanCardSynths) before the Workspace reopens: card synths that were added, replaced or removed take effect without a restart. Card master effects are listed again too. Modules the boot loaded for good (slot effects only) stay as they are, so a changed one still needs a restart.

A synth module's .otm carries its hot row: the functions that do most of its work, hottest first, from tools/hot_rows/<module>.hot. When the image has a fast block in SRAM_L, the loader shares it between the loaded synths and copies as much of each row there as its share holds; the rest runs from the slower pool. The rows come from every mode of every synth under the QEMU bench (profiles/allsynths.toml): run make hot-rows after changing a synth's DSP code, and commit the new rows. A row function the module build no longer has is reported by make card and simply stays in the slower pool.

Shared fast pool (the default when the profile compiles in a synth with a hot row): the built-in synths join in. Each built-in synth with a hot row keeps one section per function (OT_FASTRUN_ROW=1), and its row runs from flash, laid out back to back (tools/hot_pool.py layout). The SRAM_L block that the synths' .fastrun code used to take (13,696 B) is the fast block. All the project's synths take turns for it, built in or from the card, in slot order. A built-in row moves into its share when the slots change (Open, or a Model change while stopped). Its calls back into flash go through stubs, and its tables and vtable pointer follow it (src/core/modules/hot_rows.h). A row with no room keeps running from flash: slower, never wrong. The image links twice with --emit-relocs. tools/hot_pool.py table writes the move tables from the first link, and the second link must give the same ones. The table step lists what still reaches a row from flash only. That code runs the flash copy (for example PERC's snare path). On the device, the pool cut card synths' cost per voice by 22-29 % and the built-in synths' by 1-7 %, with 160 B more stack headroom (#21). Changing a synth while stopped re-shares the block, which cuts synth notes still ringing.

VERSION defaults to the Makefile's value, which follows the last upstream merge, so leave it unset unless you need a different one. This writes build/full/opentracker.elf, build/full/opentracker.hex and the flashable image build/full/PolyendTrackerOTv<digits>.ptf (e.g. PolyendTrackerOTv300.ptf for 3.0.0; the letter after OT is the profile's variant, v for full).

Change VERSION? Run make clean first

Objects aren't rebuilt when only VERSION changes, so the image would report the old version. Check with strings build/full/opentracker.elf | grep -x <version>.

The image name must be exactly 24 characters (the update bootloader rejects other lengths), so it carries the version digits only.

docs.title: Build options
docs.text: Option Builds OT_STACK_GUARD_TEST=1 a stack guard test image: with /Firmware/ot_guardtest.txt on the card it overflows the stack once on purpose, and the next boot logs PASSED / FAILED; build dir build/full/guardtest OT_HOT_POOL=0 the old layout without the shared fast pool: each built-in synth's .fastrun code in SRAM_L, card synths in the slower pool (see above); build dir build/<profile>/nopool. The fallback image when testing a boot-layout change SELFTEST=1 a hardware bring-up image that always runs the selftest OT_SDRAM_CACHE=0, OT_FASTRUN=0, OT_USB_MSC=0 diagnostic variants (no SDRAM cache, all audio code in flash, no USB mass storage)

docs.title: Size checks
docs.text:
python3 tools/telemetry_check.py size --size-tool arm-none-eabi-size build/full/opentracker.elf
python3 tools/telemetry_check.py frames build/full
make budget   # the profile's module flash budgets
  • Flash (.text + .data): fails above 832,000 B, warns above 720,000 B (upstream fails at 720,000 B; the fork's remote control and Performance mode need more; raised from 800,000 B in 2026-11 for the upstream 3.x merge, see docs/dev/memory.md). The image itself may not pass 877,664 B, the stock 1.9.2 extent (tools/check_image.py).
  • Stack headroom (_estack − _ebss): fails below 75 KiB.
  • libm: fails if double-precision math functions get linked.
  • Frames: fails if any single function's stack frame is as large as the stack guard (8 KB) or unbounded, warns above 75 % of it.

docs.title: Host tests
docs.text:
The core (src/core) is platform-independent and tested on the host with a C++17 compiler (CI uses GCC 14, with AddressSanitizer and UBSan):

make host-test

It builds and runs the tests on every core (nproc); HOST_JOBS=N sets the number of jobs, HOST_JOBS=1 runs them one by one.

On some kernels AddressSanitizer needs sudo sysctl -w vm.mmap_rnd_bits=28. A newer GCC can miss warnings that GCC 14 reports (CI builds with -Werror); to reproduce CI exactly: make -C tests CXX="g++ -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2".

docs.title: Simulator
docs.text:
make -C sim
build/full/sim/opentracker-sim

Needs SDL2 (and ALSA for MIDI). See Simulator.

docs.title: Test songs
docs.text:
make testsongs

Builds nine OT Test songs and seven BLAST GRID synth remixes into build/testsongs/. Copy its Projects/ and Samples/ folders to a card.

docs.title: Performance gate
docs.text:
make perf-gate [LOG=tracker.log]

Instruction counts of the audio engine on an emulated Cortex-M4 (QEMU) against tests/perf_baseline.txt (+5 % max) and per-engine limits, the flash and stack checks, a host benchmark, and, with LOG=, the telemetry thresholds of a device log. Needs qemu-system-arm for the M4 part (skipped otherwise). Run it for anything on the audio path. CI runs it too (the perf-gate job, with QEMU and Arm's 14.2.Rel1). The baseline is recorded with that compiler: another gcc counts a few percent differently, so record a new baseline only from a 14.2.Rel1 build.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text: This site is built from docs/ in the repository with MkDocs and the Material theme, and published to GitHub Pages by .github/workflows/docs.yml.

docs.title: Edit and preview
docs.text:
Docs change in the same pull request as the feature they describe.

python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install "mkdocs<2" mkdocs-material mike
python3 tools/docs_synth_pages.py  # the Synths pages, from ../opentracker-synths
.venv/bin/mkdocs serve            # http://127.0.0.1:8000, reloads on save
.venv/bin/mkdocs build --strict   # what CI runs: broken links fail

Pages are listed in mkdocs.yml (nav:). Images go in docs/images/.

docs.title: Screenshots
docs.text:
Screenshots come from the simulator, so they can be regenerated whenever a screen changes:

make testsongs && make -C sim
tools/docs_screens.sh            # all of them, or: tools/docs_screens.sh song performance

Each shot in tools/docs_screens.sh is a short simulator script run on a fresh scratch card: either the generated test songs with "BG World 1" open, or an empty project with a generated example DX7 bank. No third-party content goes into the images.

docs.title: Versions
docs.text:
Publishing uses mike, which keeps one copy of the site per version on the gh-pages branch:

  • every push to main updates dev;
  • every release tag (v*, the same tags that make a release) adds its own version, named after the tag, and moves the latest alias to it. The site opens on latest, so readers get the docs for the firmware they can download; the version picker at the top switches to dev or an older release.

A release's Synths pages come from the synth repository's main at the time of the tag, as its card modules do (release.yml).

docs.title: Synth help files
docs.text:
Each synth's help lives next to its code in the module repository, modules/<synth>/help/<NAME>.md (NAME = the descriptor's name, e.g. BTYPE): a guide for the docs, then the # Settings reference that the Edit Patch help box reads (format in src/core/modules/synth_help.h, user view in Edit Patch and synth help).

  • make help (and make firmware) writes the card copies, the reference only, to build/<profile>/Help/Synths/ (tools/synth_help_card.py); the release puts them in Modules.zip.
  • tools/docs_synth_pages.py [MODULES_DIR] writes the Synths pages of this site, docs/synths/ (not in git): the whole file per synth, the reference one heading level down, and an overview. The docs workflow runs it on the synth repository's main; run it once before mkdocs serve. A new synth also needs its line in mkdocs.yml.
  • make host-test (tests/synth_help_test.cpp) checks every help file of the profile's modules against the descriptor: names, full coverage, no markup, the widest font fits.
  • Config's help box texts work the same way: help/Config.md in this repository (## a category, ### an option), on the card as Help/Config.md; tests/config_screen_test.cpp checks it against the Config menu.
  • Describe what a setting does. Wording about how something sounds goes in only after it has been heard on the device.

docs.title: OpenTracker memory audit: fork vs upstream 2.1.2
docs.text: 2026-10-23. Measured from the ELF images (Games off) and on a Tracker over the remote-control link. Fork: syamajala/polyend-tracker-re main (a8ac7b4, on 2.1.1); upstream: sandlbn/polyend-tracker-re v2 at 2.1.2 (177150b). Fork figures corrected the same day from clean builds: the first version listed the fork's room above _ebss as upstream's.

docs.title: Flash on 2026-11-11
docs.text:
main b2bec6e (3.x, gcc 14.2), full: 794,624 B (.text 787,796 + .data 6,828); upstream v3 13438f6: 737,280 B. The upstream 3.x merge comes to 806,912 B, so the fork's flash gate went from 800,000 to 832,000 B. The image cap stays tools/check_image.py's stock extent (877,664 B).

  • Strings: 34.9 KB merged pool (about 1,900 strings): help texts ~14 KB, printf formats ~7.7 KB (mostly hardware diagnostics), short labels ~13 KB. Most are in upstream files. The map shows the whole pool under ff.c (its first .str1.1 section), so per-object sums put "35 KB rodata" there.
  • Fork over upstream: ~51 KB of code and data. Performance mode +12.2 KB in screen_performance.cpp (scene banks ~2.7 KB, A/B scenes ~3.8 KB, Fader Ranges ~1.75 KB, MIDI CC type list ~1.15 KB, growth of upstream functions ~2 KB; plus the bank and scene side files), remote control 8.8 KB, progressions 5.4 KB, SFZ / multisample 5.5 KB, export resampler 4.7 KB.
  • LTO over the whole image: -16.4 KB, but the card-module exports, the hot pool row tables and the audio path all change; not taken. LTO over the -Os files only is untried.

docs.title: Fork main on 2026-11-01
docs.text:
Re-measured from main bc714a8 (Games off), after USB audio, multisample, scene bank files, fader ranges and the SDRAM sharing of #109. The tables below are the 2026-10-23 audit and are kept for the comparison with upstream.

2026-10-23 2026-11-01 Flash (.text + .data) — 774,144 B (fail then > 800,000 B: ~26 KB left) SRAM .bss 98,284 B 109,492 B Room above _ebss (heap + stack) 92,448 B 79,104 B Margin over the 75 KiB stack rule 15,648 B 2,304 B .sdram_bss used (148 KB region) 90,960 B 129,344 B .sdram_bss free 60,592 B 22,208 B
  • Flash audit (#122, 2026-11-05): 790,528 → 774,144 B (the gate number, which counts the 4 KB-aligned zero padding after .data); 778,240 B once our own float printf came back (2026-11-06).
  • Our own float printf (−12 KB, +1.3 KB): newlib's %f (dtoa, mprec and their soft-double helpers) is no longer linked. newlib-nano calls a weak _printf_float for every float conversion; src/hal/printf_float.cpp defines it with fm::formatFloat() (src/core/float_format.h), which prints glibc's digits from 64-bit integers: exact for |v| < 1e9 with up to 9 decimals, %e / %g as %f. So %f works on the device, in our code and in modules, and the call sites read as upstream's (#131's fm::fixed is reverted). The firmware link fails without the hook (%f would print nothing), and telemetry_check.py size fails if newlib's _dtoa_r comes back. make host-test also runs make -C tests printf-m4: the toolchain's own snprintf with the hook under QEMU, diffed against glibc, so a newlib that changes the hook's arguments fails there.
  • DX7 sine table built at boot (−4 KB): gDx7Sin is no longer copied from flash; dx7::initSinTable() runs msfa's integer recipe (~60 µs). Since #21 DX7 is a card module (opentracker-synths modules/dx7): its code (~18 KB) left the image and the table (4.1 KB) is the module's bss in the card pool, built in attach().
  • Looked at, left: ~36 KB of string literals (mostly Config help text), fonts (already compressed), the play-mode tables (~1.3 KB if packed).
  • SRAM is tight again. USB audio is about half of the drop (~7 KB: its rings and buffers stay in SRAM because the USB interrupt and the audio block both touch them); the rest is spread over other features. Nothing moves from SDRAM back to SRAM unless the 75 KiB rule is lowered; the real stack peak is still ~18 KB.
  • .sdram_bss options left, each with a cost: the Sample Loader's name pool (25.8 KB; shrinking it to 16 KB saves ~10 KB but long-name folders lose entries), folding Recents, the text scratch and the multisample staging buffer into g_io (~10 KB, needs a lifetime audit), FF_FS_TINY for the 7.2 KB of file handles (a streaming-speed risk). The remote bridge (7.3 KB) stays.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• Upstream is at its limits on both RAMs. It has 1,104 B free in .sdram_bss and 1,280 B over its 90 KiB stack rule.
  • Most of that pressure is fixed cost, not features. A per-screen buffer for each browser list, the screens on the SRAM heap, and a stack rule set without measurement account for tens of KB.
  • The fork's fixed SRAM is about 1 KB more than upstream's (169,412 B vs 168,420 B), even with its extra features. Our margin comes from measuring the real stack use, putting the screens in SDRAM and sharing the browser buffers.
  • Ready to merge: branch feature/sdram-shared-lists (off upstream/v2, two commits) frees 16 KB of .sdram_bss and 8.4 KB of heap on upstream.
  • These fixes don't need a module system. They are independent of the modular-architecture discussion and can land first. A module system mainly helps flash (features in or out of a build); on its own it doesn't reduce these fixed RAM costs.

docs.title: SRAM (256 KB)
docs.text:
Upstream 2.1.2 Fork main Audio code run from SRAM (.fastrun) 40,248 B 41,424 B Other initialised data 2,904 B 7,016 B .bss 102,580 B 98,284 B DMA + USB buffers 22,688 B 22,688 B Fixed SRAM total 168,420 B 169,412 B Room above _ebss (heap + stack) 93,440 B 92,448 B Link-time stack rule (STACK_MIN) 92,160 B (90 KiB) 76,800 B (75 KiB) Margin over the rule 1,280 B 15,648 B Screens (ScreenSet) on the heap 15,884 B 0 (in SDRAM) Stack guard + heap reserve — 12,288 B Stack really left at run time ~77.5 KB ~80 KB

Measured on a Tracker (fork, stack painting + telemetry):

Value Deepest stack use 18,084 B (long session: project load and play, Sample Editor effects, Save / Save As, resample, USB storage) Typical 11–12.5 KB Heap 232 B once the screens are in SDRAM Deepest single frame 6,032 B (-fstack-usage, every function)

So about 60 KB of the stack is never touched. The 90 KiB rule is what's tight, not the stack itself.

docs.title: SDRAM (16 MB)
docs.text:
The fixed layout is the same in both: about 11.25 MB of sample pool, 1.56 MB for delay and reverb, and patterns, undo, clipboard, Performance, stems and the remote frame buffer. It ends a little below .sdram_bss.

.sdram_bss Upstream 2.1.2 Upstream + sdram-shared-lists Fork main today Region 92 KB @ 0x70FD9000 92 KB 148 KB @ 0x70FDB000 Used 93,104 B 77,056 B 90,960 B Free 1,104 B 17,152 B 60,592 B Unused SDRAM above the region 64 KB 64 KB 0

The SDRAM above the region is used only by the self-test's SD benchmark, which never runs alongside the app.

docs.title: Recommendations for upstream, by payoff
docs.text:
1. Merge feature/sdram-shared-lists (a034a95, 6b0ccaa).
  2. Shared browser lists: the Sample Loader, Synth patch browser, File Open/Save, Import Mod and firmware-update lists share one buffer (browserListMem(), 11,400 B). Only one is ever on screen, and each rebuilds its list when it opens.
  3. One screenshot row buffer: the row is converted to BMP bytes in place.
  4. Result: .sdram_bss −16,048 B, heap −8.4 KB, flash −344 B. All 91 upstream test suites and make -C sim check pass. In the fork it's device-tested by a remote script that visits every list (24 checks).
  5. Screens in SDRAM (fork 928db9d, feature/screens-sdram). ScreenSet moves from the heap into .sdram_bss, which frees the remaining ~7.5 KB of heap after step 1. Device-tested: render and loop times were identical while browsing a 578-file folder with previews.
  6. Base the stack rule on measurement.
  7. Measure: paint the stack and report the peak in telemetry.
  8. Guard: add a SYSMPU guard below the stack (fork #34: 8 KB; an overflow locks up the core, resets, and is reported on the next boot).
  9. Check frames: a CI check that fails if a single frame could jump over the guard (telemetry_check.py frames).
  10. Then lower the rule. The fork went from 90 to 75 KiB, which frees about 15 KB of SRAM at link time without moving anything.
  11. Keep the Open's Project off the stack, with one spare copy (fork ac02790, with 51d9f57). Upstream keeps a Project on the stack in startOpenProject and in the Workspace load step, plus ProjectJob::proj. One SDRAM jobProject_ outside the job state replaces all three. That's no extra SDRAM, two big stack frames fewer, and one copy fewer.
  12. Grow .sdram_bss into the unused 64 KB above it. It's a linker-script and board.h size change, plus a static_assert that the region stays below the end of SDRAM.

Only if SRAM is still needed:

Candidate Saves Condition Instruments to SDRAM ~17 KB Read at note-on; needs a CPU check SD bounce buffer ~16 KB Only once SDHC → SDRAM DMA is verified Diagnostic log ring ~8 KB Shrink it, or move it after boot .fastrun code back to flash varies Each piece costs audio CPU

docs.title: Tools used
docs.text:
• tools/size_report.py: flash, SRAM sections, .sdram_bss, stack headroom and free space, base vs head. Runs as a CI job summary on every PR.
  • tools/telemetry_check.py:
  • size: the link-time limits;
  • frames: the deepest frame vs the stack guard;
  • log: stack peak, heap, CPU and overruns from a device log.
  • -fstack-usage on every build; pahole -C <type> build/full/opentracker.elf for struct layouts.
  • Remote-control scripts (tools/remote_scripts/*.txt), run on the simulator in CI and on a Tracker with the telemetry log captured.

docs.title: Simulator
docs.text:
The desktop simulator runs the same platform-independent core (src/core) as the firmware on Linux, with host implementations of the hardware interfaces: an SDL2 window with the screen, pads and keys, audio out, ALSA MIDI, and a folder as the SD card. Most features can be developed and tested without flashing.

The full reference is sim/README.md.

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
make -C sim
build/full/sim/opentracker-sim [--sd DIR] [--scale 2] [--line-in]
  • --sd DIR is the SD card root (default ~/.opentracker-sd, created on first run). The workspace is saved there when the window closes; Config is kept in DIR.eeprom.
  • Keyboard: F1–F8 are the screen keys, arrows, Space = Play, Shift, Delete, Page Up / Down = encoder. Tab switches between command mode (letters = module keys, e.g. 2 Performance, 0 Song) and pad mode (letter rows = pads). The mouse works on every control; right-click latches a button (e.g. Shift).
  • --usb-in NAME stands in for USB audio from the computer (USB audio): a capture device, e.g. the monitor of a null sink the browser plays into (--usb-in list prints the names; see sim/README.md). --usb-in-tone HZ is the headless version.
  • --usb-out NAME plays the USB send (what the computer would record) on another output device. Headless scripts use usb-out on|off and expect-usb-out / expect-usb-out-quiet instead.

docs.title: Scripts
docs.text:
Without a window (--script FILE and/or --screenshot OUT.png), time is virtual: every simulated millisecond is one app loop pass, so runs are deterministic and fast.

wait 300               # advance time (ms)
tap PERFORMANCE        # press and release a button (names: src/core/ui/buttons.h)
press SHIFT / release SHIFT
hold F5 400
pad 12 tap             # pads 0..47
enc 3                  # encoder detents
screenshot perf.png

Plus checks (expect-screen, expect-sound, expect-playing …) and --wav OUT.wav to record the audio. make -C sim check runs the simulator's own checks.

docs.title: Display budgets
docs.text: The Tracker's display chip (FT813) has a small display-list memory (RAM_DL). The budget and fragcheck commands in sim/scripts/display_budget.txt and fork_screens.txt measure each screen's largest frame and check it looks identical with the fragment cache on and off. A new or changed screen needs an entry there.

docs.title: Standing in for a Tracker
docs.text:
• --serve acts like a Tracker with remote control on, on a pseudo-terminal, so tools/tracker_remote.py scripts run against it (CI does this).
  • --remote DEV and --mirror DEV use a real Tracker as the panel or show its screen: see Remote control.

docs.title: Testing and CI
docs.text: The rule of thumb: test in the simulator and on the host first, and use the device for what only hardware shows (sound quality and clicks, real CPU and stack use, pads and LEDs, the codec and Line in, SD timing). Batch device tests so one flash covers several changes.

docs.title: Layers
docs.text: Layer Command Covers Host tests make host-test ~100 test binaries: models, formats, sequencer, audio engines, UI screens, display budgets (ASan + UBSan) Simulator checks make -C sim check smoke runs, display budgets and fragment checks per screen, resampling end to end, the test songs open and play Remote scripts tools/sim_remote_check.sh tools/remote_scripts/*.txt against the simulator, each on a fresh card; the same files run on a Tracker M4 benchmark make perf-gate audio instruction counts on an emulated Cortex-M4 against a baseline, engine limits, size checks Device tools/tracker_remote.py, tools/telemetry_check.py log scripts and telemetry on a real Tracker

docs.title: Music theory cases
docs.text:
Chord names and notes the tests expect (progressions, chord hints) are rows in tests/theory_cases.inc, so they aren't taken from our own code: the host tests read the rows, and tools/theory_check/check.mjs checks the same rows against the Tonal library (letter spelling, chord notes, minor keys with harmonic minor's leading tone). After adding or changing a row:

cd tools/theory_check && npm ci && node check.mjs

It needs Node and the network for npm ci, so it isn't part of make host-test. Tonal only checks the theory: how a progression's key is picked and where it plays in a project scale are our own rules, tested in tests/progression_test.cpp.

docs.title: Remote scripts
docs.text:
Scripts in tools/remote_scripts/ drive the app through tracker_remote.py and are written to run on both the simulator and a Tracker:

  • Wait on the sequencer, not the clock: wait-for pass == 2, wait-for slot == 3 20000, so a script works at any tempo.
  • A script's card starts with SCRIPT.sd/ (copy it to a Tracker's card too) and, in the simulator only, SCRIPT.sim-sd/.
  • Open projects with open FOLDER/NAME (@RC DO OPEN, src/core/remote/remote.h), not with File screen keys (remote_calls.txt shows it). tools/pool_bench.sh uses it to play the 16 pool songs on a Tracker with no hands on it.

On a device:

tools/tracker_remote.py /dev/ttyACM0 tools/remote_scripts/song_scene.txt --log tracker.log
tools/telemetry_check.py log tracker.log

tools/device_soak.txt is a navigation-only soak for a loaded project (no edits, saves or loads).

Gotchas when writing scripts:

  • Opening the Sample Recorder while a pattern plays pops a "stop the pattern?" dialog (Resample / Cancel / Yes) that takes the F keys. Stop playback first, or answer it.
  • Config reopens on the category it was last on, so start from a known place (e.g. Up × 7).
  • On a device, the diag ring drops early boot lines. Send a byte on the CDC port to replay the boot log.

docs.title: Hardware probes
docs.text:
A test image built with make OT_REMOTE_REGS=1 also answers register commands in drive mode, so hardware questions can be answered with a script instead of a special image. Release images (the default OT_REMOTE_REGS=0) answer every one of them with FAIL.

Script command Does Limited to peek ADDR [N] read N (1..8) MCU words GPIO, PORT, SIM, SRAM, flash (other peripherals fault when their clock is off) poke ADDR VALUE write an MCU word a PORTx_PCRn switching between disabled and GPIO input: a pin can never be made to drive ftrd ADDR [N] read N (1..32) bytes of display memory the FT81x memory map ftwr ADDR VALUE [BYTES] write a display register the register block, not REG_CPURESET or the coprocessor's FIFO pointers

Addresses and values are hex without 0x; the rules are in src/core/remote/remote.h. Python scripts can call Runner.peek / poke / ftrd / ftwr from tracker_remote.py. tools/int_n_probe.py uses them to find out whether the FT81x INT_N pin reaches the MCU (it toggles the pin and reads every port, then restores everything).

docs.title: CI
docs.text:
Pull requests and pushes to main run .github/workflows/ci.yml (other branches: Run workflow on the Actions tab):

Job Does host-tests make host-test with GCC 14, plus telemetry_check.py selftest sim-check builds the simulator, make -C sim check, the remote scripts; uploads screenshots firmware builds the image, size / stack / libm checks, the stack frame check; uploads the .ptf as an artifact size-report pull requests only: memory use of the PR against its base, as a table in the job summary

Error messages are shown as annotations on the run, so they're visible without opening the logs.

docs.title: Releases
docs.text: Pushing a tag vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH[-suffix] (e.g. v2.1.2-ot1) runs .github/workflows/release.yml: host tests, the firmware with the size checks, and a GitHub release with the .ptf image. The image uses the numeric version only (v2.1.2-ot1 → PolyendTrackerOTv212.ptf); the suffix names the release.

docs.title: Branches
docs.text:
• main is the fork's integration branch: what gets flashed and released. It's on upstream's 3.x (synth and FX modules, build profiles) and never rebased; upstream's v3 is merged into it.
  • main-v2 is the fork on upstream 2.x, as it was when main moved to 3.x (2026-11-08). It's kept for reference and gets no upstream merges.
  • v2 mirrors upstream's v2 (sandlbn/polyend-tracker-re) and is fast-forwarded when upstream moves.
  • Feature branches come into main through pull requests on the fork, with CI. A change meant for upstream starts from upstream/v3 (or upstream/v2 for a 2.x fix), so it can be offered upstream as it is; fork-only work (card modules, song scenes …) starts from main.
  • Upstream pull requests are opened one at a time. Upstream squash-merges, so a branch stacked on another is rebased after the first one lands.

docs.title: Merging upstream
docs.text:
1. Update the module repositories (opentracker-synths, opentracker-fx) to upstream's main, since upstream v3 can depend on module changes.
  2. Merge upstream/v3 into a branch off main, resolve, then build with make clean, run the host tests, make -C sim check and tools/sim_remote_check.sh. Upstream merges its v2 fixes into v3, so they arrive this way too. Check a v3 merge for deletions of fork work (git diff main <merge>): upstream's first v3 snapshot rolled back some 2.2.x work.
  3. Open a pull request into main; flash it together with whatever else waits for a device test.

When upstream squash-merged one of our own pull requests, its conflicts resolve to our side, and only upstream's other changes need applying on top (git diff <their squash> <their release>).

docs.title: Compatibility rules
docs.text:
Projects must keep opening in stock firmware, upstream OpenTracker and the Tracker Mini:

  • Stock files keep their layout. project.mt, pattern files, .pti instruments and .patch files are written exactly as the stock / Mini formats define them.
  • Fork data goes into side files next to project.mt, which other firmware ignores:
File Holds perf_scenes.bin the Performance scene bank, A / B, and the fork's column types (DJ filter, tape stop, MIDI CC), MIDI CC targets and the fader ranges (#12) song.bin per-slot Count, Scene, Scene B and Ramp midi_lfo.bin one LFO per MIDI instrument usb_audio.bin the Global Mixer USB level and mute, and whether the Sample Recorder records USB timing.bin each pattern's per-track Speed and Groove (#43 / #83), one record per pattern off the defaults multisample.bin the root notes of each multisample instrument's zones and whether it plays in Multi mode (the .pti is a plain Slice instrument) .patch field 100 a DX7 voice (155 bytes), past every Mini field
  • Side files are versioned and written only when they hold something. The fork has no installed base yet, so their layouts can still change without migration code; stock compatibility can't.
  • A new Performance column type is not written into project.mt's type bytes (stock reads them); it lives in perf_scenes.bin, and stock sees an empty column.
  • Files on the card outside a project are text, so people can edit them on a computer: MidiPresets/<name>.txt (formats/midi_preset.h) and Performance/Scenes/<name>.txt scene banks (formats/perf_bank.h). Both use key = value lines, # comments and ignore unknown keys, so later versions can add keys. The shipped MIDI presets are in midi_presets/; host tests parse each one.
  • Progressions/<Group>.txt (Song mode progressions, ui/progression.h) is one progression per line in scale numbers, not key = value. The built-in files are compiled in (prog::defaultText) and written only when the folder has no .txt file, never over an existing one.
  • Themes/<name>.json are Tracker CE's colour themes, read and written in CE's format so themes move between CE's web editor and OpenTracker (ui/theme_file.h). The CE key -> slot map is generated: edit tools/ce_theme_map.py and run it to rewrite src/core/ui/ce_theme_map.inc. The map came from black-box observation only: a theme with one colour per CE key was screenshotted in CE's web editor and matched pixel by pixel against the simulator with one colour per slot. Slots 277..284 are fork slots for parts CE colours apart from the stock sets; the stock themes copy the colour each one replaces. The example themes are in themes/; host tests parse each one.

docs.title: Code conventions
docs.text:
• src/core is platform-independent (shared by the firmware, the simulator and the host tests); src/hal is the K66 hardware layer.
  • Comments mark the origin of behaviour: [I] the fork's own (not in stock), spec references (spec 12 §E.2) for reverse-engineered stock behaviour.
  • The audio path has no allocation, no I/O and no locks. Anything on it goes through make perf-gate; new screens get a display budget entry.
  • No static constructors: a namespace-scope object or pointer must not need dynamic initialisation (for example T* const p = f(); with f() in another file). Use constexpr, an extern array with inline helpers, or set it up in start(). Check with arm-none-eabi-nm -C build/full/opentracker.elf | grep _GLOBAL__sub_I.

docs.title: DX7 synth
docs.text: A 6-operator FM engine that plays Yamaha DX7 voices, a synth model next to ACD, FAT, VAP, WTFM and PERC. Thousands of free DX7 voices exist as SysEx (.syx) files; the Tracker plays them directly.

docs.title: Install it
docs.text:
DX7 comes as a file on the SD card rather than in the firmware, which leaves room for other features:

  1. Copy dx7.otm (in Modules.zip on the release page) into Modules/ on the SD card.
  2. Restart the Tracker, or if you copied the file in USB storage mode, just leave USB storage mode. DX7 now shows in the Model list. It loads when a project uses it: pick it as the Model and it's ready a moment later (while the song plays, it loads when you press Stop).

Without the file, a project that uses DX7 still opens, with the notice "Synth 1 (DX7) not available"; put the file back to play it.

DX7 takes about 18 KB of the card memory (about 45 KB) that card synths and card effects share, so with DX7 loaded not every effect fits. Config > Memory shows what is loaded.

docs.title: Use a DX7 voice
docs.text:
1. Put .syx files in Patches/DX7/ on the SD card. Both kinds work:
    • 32-voice banks (4,104 bytes, the usual "bank" files);
    • single-voice dumps (163 bytes).
  2. Select a synth instrument (S1–S3): hold Instrument and turn the encoder.
  3. Press Instrument Params. On Synth Parameters, set Model to DX7 (after the built-in models in the list).
  4. Press Load Patch (F7).
  1. Banks come first in the list and open like folders: highlight one and press Open (F8). Pick a voice, Preview (F5, hold) to hear it, Confirm (F8) to load it. Left goes back to the bank list. Single-voice files sit with the patches and preview and load directly.

The loaded voice is named after the DX7 voice. Save (in Edit Patch) writes it as an ordinary .patch file in Patches/DX7/, with the voice stored inside it; the project keeps it too.

docs.title: Shape a voice
docs.text:
There's no operator editor yet, but Edit Patch has controls that work on top of any loaded voice, without changing the voice itself:

Section Control What it does Voice Volume The voice's level. Voice Mono For polyphony 1 slots: Retrigger (default) or Legato, see below. Tone Brightness ±100 %: the modulators' levels, ±12 dB. More or fewer harmonics. Tone Feedback ±7, added to the voice's own feedback (0–7). Tone Attack ±100 %: every operator's first envelope rate. + = slower. Tone Release ±100 %: every operator's release rate. + = longer tails. Tone LFO Depth 0–200 % of the voice's vibrato and tremolo, up to the DX7's maximum. Tone Detune 0–100 %: spreads the operators up to ±7 cents apart (chorus-like beating).

Each loaded DX7 voice comes with macros M1–M6 aimed at the six Tone controls and named after them (M1 Bright, M2 Feedback … M6 Detune). So a voice can be shaped from the Synth Macros page (Instrument Params again), or per step with the macro FX (columns A–F), without opening Edit Patch. To aim them elsewhere, use F4 To Macro and the Macros section in Edit Patch.

How much a control changes depends on the voice: Brightness does nothing on a voice without modulators, and Feedback is only heard when the feedback operator is audible.

docs.title: Playing
docs.text:
• DX7 slots play from any track like the other synths: notes, the step FX for pitch (Glide, Slide, Tune, Micro-tune), the Volume FX and the macro FX.
  • Polyphony is set on Synth Parameters. On a polyphony 1 slot, Mono decides what a new note does:
    • Retrigger (default): every note starts like a new voice, its envelopes from the beginning (without a click).
    • Legato: a note that overlaps the held one only moves the pitch; the envelopes run on, as on a DX7 in mono mode.
  • Velocity (the Volume step FX on a step with a note) works as on a DX7: through each operator's velocity sensitivity in the voice. On some voices it changes the level, on others mostly the tone (a velocity-sensitive modulator gets brighter with velocity). Voices whose operators have sensitivity 0 ignore it. To make one respond in level anyway, aim M7 (Velocity) at Volume on its Edit Patch page.
    • A Volume FX on a step without a note doesn't change a held DX7 note: velocity only counts when a note starts.
  • CPU: about 6 % per voice (estimated). The voice limiter cuts synth voices first if the audio gets close to its limit.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• The sound core is a port of Google's Music Synthesizer for Android (msfa, Apache 2.0), checked against Dexed note by note. Our additions: amplitude modulation, the feedback loops of algorithms 4 and 6, and key sync.
  • For deeper edits, edit the voice in a DX7 editor on a computer (Dexed works) and copy the .syx file over.
  • A Tracker Mini has no DX7 model: it resets a DX7 slot to its default when it opens the project.

docs.title: Edit Patch and synth help
docs.text: Edit Patch (Instrument Params on a synth slot, then F8) shows every setting of the slot's synth. In this fork it's laid out like Config, and a help box explains whatever you're on.

docs.title: The layout
docs.text:
Three columns, left to right:

Column Shows Sections the synth's groups of settings (Channel, Envelope …), then Macros Settings the settings of the selected section, with their values Value the selected setting's value: a list of choices, or a bar for a number
  • Left / Right move the red frame from column to column.
  • Up / Down and the knob move inside the framed column: in the value column they change the setting. In a list, Down goes down the list; on a bar, Up raises the value.
  • F5 / F7 move to the previous / next setting and F6 to the next section, wherever the frame is.
  • Delete puts the selected setting back to its Init value.
  • F1 Save, F2 Save As, F3 Init Patch and F8 Back work as before.
  • F4 To Macro puts the selected setting on a macro (below).
  • All 48 pads play the synth while you edit (stock picks the section with the pads).

docs.title: Macros
docs.text:
A macro is one knob that moves several settings at once: M1–M6 are the knobs on the Synth Macros page (Instrument Params again) and the pattern's FX columns A–F, M7 follows the Volume column. With a macro at +1.00 on a setting, turning the knob all the way up moves that setting across its whole range; −1.00 moves it the other way.

Put a setting on a macro: select the setting, press F4 To Macro. The value column lists M1–M6 with how many settings each one moves, and on where this setting already is. Pick one with Up / Down or the knob and press F4 again: Add puts the setting on it at +1.00, Remove takes it off. F8 cancels. A macro without a name of its own takes the setting's name. A macro moves at most five settings.

The Macros section, the last in the list, shows every macro with the settings it moves:

  • On a macro's row: Unipolar (the knob goes from 0 up) or Bipolar (the middle is 0) in the value column; F8 Rename names it.
  • On one of its settings: the amount in the value column, −2.00 to +2.00; F3 Remove takes the setting off the macro; Delete puts the amount back to the Init patch's.

The Synth Macros page lists under each bar the settings its macro moves, with + or − for the direction, or "not set".

An Init patch starts with no macros set; DX7 voices come with M1–M6 on the six Tone controls (see DX7).

docs.title: The help box
docs.text:
Under the columns, three lines:

  1. the section: what the group is for;
  2. the setting: what it does;
  3. the choice you're on, or for a number, what low and high values do.

For example, on B-Type's Channel > Distortion with Poly5: "Channel: the main voice, a chip square wave and how buzzy it is", "Distortion: how the square is shaped", "Poly5: a 5-step pattern".

The texts come from the SD card, Help/Synths/<SYNTH>.md (in Modules.zip on the release page, next to the card modules; see Install the modules). Without the file the box says which one is missing, and everything else works as usual.

Every synth has a help file. The same text, with a guide to how each synth works, is on its page under Synths.

docs.title: Writing a help file
docs.text:
Each synth's help is a Markdown file next to its code in the module repository, modules/<synth>/help/<SYNTH>.md. It has two parts:

  • a guide for these docs (how the synth works, tips), free Markdown;
  • # Settings, the short reference the help box shows: ## a section, ### a setting, - Choice: text for each choice, named exactly as on screen, with one short paragraph under each heading.

Only the reference goes on the card; the whole file becomes the synth's page on this site. make host-test checks it against the synth: every section, setting and choice needs a line, and each line has to fit the box. The format is in src/core/modules/synth_help.h.

docs.title: Master effects
docs.text: Put an echo, chorus or tape saturation on the whole mix: press Shift + Master, pick Echo with the arrows, press Turn on (F1). It plays straight away; Edit (F2) opens its settings.

docs.title: The FX bank
docs.text:
Shift + Master opens the FX bank: every master effect, in the order the mix runs through them. Each row says On, Off, or Card (on the SD card, not loaded yet). The panel on the right shows where the selected effect lives, how much memory it takes and its place in the chain.

Key Does Up / Down, encoder Pick an effect. Turn on / Turn off (F1) Switch the selected effect. Edit (F2) Its settings page (F1–F8 pick a setting, the encoder changes it). Shift + Master From a settings page: back to the bank. From the bank: back to Master. Master The Master, Track Mixer and Global Mixer pages, as on stock.

To play an effect from the pads (on for a fill, Echo throws, a Mix sweep on the fader), give it a Master FX column in Performance mode.

docs.title: The effects
docs.text:
The mix runs through them in this order, whichever are on:

Dirt (drive) → LoFi → Chorus → BBD chorus → Echo → Tape

The order is fixed, so every project sounds the same on every Tracker.

docs.title: Effects on the card
docs.text:
The effects are card modules: copy them from Modules.zip on the release page into Modules/ on the SD card (as DX7). An effect only takes memory while it is on:

  • Turn on loads it from the card. While the song plays it loads at the next Stop (the bank says At Stop).
  • Turn off silences it at once; it leaves memory at the next Stop.
  • A project remembers its effects and their settings: opening it loads the ones that are on.
  • Echo borrows 48 KB of sample memory while it is loaded (about half a second of mono sample). Samples come first: when they fill the memory, Echo doesn't load and the bank says Not enough sample memory.
  • Card effects and card synths share the card memory (about 45 KB). When it is full, an effect doesn't load and the bank says Card memory full, naming the biggest module loaded (e.g. DX7); turn off another effect or pick a built-in synth. Config > Memory lists what is in it.

Without the Modules/ folder there are no master effects; projects still open and play.

docs.title: MIDI instrument LFO
docs.text: Each MIDI instrument (MIDI 1–16) gets one tempo-locked LFO, sent alongside its notes.

docs.title: Set it up
docs.text:
1. Select a MIDI instrument: hold Instrument and turn the encoder.
  2. Press Instrument Params, then Instrument Params again: the key steps through the MIDI parameters page, the MIDI Instrument LFO page and the MIDI Instrument Preset page.
Setting (key) Choices Target (F1) Off, one of the CC slots A–F, pitch bend or channel pressure; the whole list is on screen, slots shown by their CC's name ("A Cutoff"). The LFO follows the slot: change the slot's CC on the parameters page and the LFO moves with it. A slot set to Prg Chg or Poly AT sends nothing. Turning the encoder only picks the target; the LFO moves to it once the encoder rests, so the slots passed on the way are left alone. Shape (F2) Rev saw, Saw, Triangle, Square, Random. Rate (F3) From 128 steps per cycle down to 1/8 step, locked to the tempo. Depth (F4) How far it swings either side of Center, 0–64: Center 64 and Depth 32 sweep 32–96; Depth 64 sweeps the whole range. Center (F5) The value it swings around (0–127): value = Center + Depth × wave, kept within 0–127. On pitch bend, -64..63 around no bend, in the same steps as Depth. Retrigger (F6) Free (follows the song position) or Note (restarts with each note).

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• LFO messages use at most half of a DIN MIDI port's bandwidth, so notes are never delayed by them.
  • The LFO runs while the sequencer plays. At Stop, its target is left at Center, and so is a target you switch away from (or turn Off) while playing.
  • A step FX on the same target (the LFO's CC slot, pitch bend, or pressure) moves the LFO's Center, so the pattern can shift the wobble around.
  • Stored in midi_lfo.bin next to project.mt; other firmware ignores it.

docs.title: MIDI presets
docs.text:
A MIDI preset describes a synth: the names of its CCs (its CC chart, "74 Cutoff"), which CCs the six slots A–F use, velocity, offset and the MIDI LFO. Save it once, then load it into any MIDI instrument in any project.

The CC names show wherever a CC appears: as the slot name on the MIDI parameters page ("Cutoff" instead of "CC A"), in the CC A–F choice lists ("74 Cutoff") and as the LFO target. Step FX in the pattern still read CC A–F, as on the original firmware.

A preset describes the synth, not a sound or a channel:

  • No channel. It loads into whichever MIDI instrument is open, and that instrument's channel stays. A synth that listens on several channels (an Elektron Model:Cycles, one channel per track) uses one preset on each of them. Instruments that load the same preset share its CC chart, so a name changed on one shows on all of them.
  • No program change. To switch the synth's sound in a song, set a CC slot to Prg Chg and put that FX on a step.

docs.title: The Preset page
docs.text:
1. Select a MIDI instrument: hold Instrument and turn the encoder.
  2. Press Instrument Params until the title reads MIDI Instrument Preset (it steps through Parameters, LFO and Preset).

The left list is the CC chart: CC 0–127 with their names, and the letters of the slots that use each CC. It opens on slot A's CC. The right side shows the preset this instrument came from or was saved as, and the six slots.

Key Action Encoder, Up / Down Select a CC (hold Shift to move faster). F6 Name Name the selected CC (up to 9 characters). Delete Clear the selected CC's name. F1 Load List the presets on the card; the encoder or Up / Down move, F8 Load loads into this instrument, F7 Cancel closes the list. F2 Save Save under the preset's name (no name yet: as Save As). F3 Save As Save under a new name (asks before replacing a preset).

Which CC a slot uses is set on the MIDI parameters page, as before. The names and the preset name are saved with the project (midi_names.bin, next to project.mt), so project.mt stays readable by the original firmware. A project holds up to 400 CC names in all (about eight fully named synths).

docs.title: Presets that come with OpenTracker
docs.text:
Each release has a MidiPresets.zip: unzip it to the root of the card. It holds:

Preset Channels Slots A–F Model Cycles one per track (load it on each) Color, Shape, Sweep, Contour, Decay, Delay send Syntakt audio tracks 1–12 (Syn A–H = the machine's parameters) Cutoff, Reso, Filter env, Amp decay, Delay send, Reverb send Syntakt FX the FX track Filter freq, Filter reso, Drive, Delay mix, Reverb mix, Delay time volca fm2 its channel (needs MIDI RX ShortMessage on) Mod decay, Carrier decay, Algorithm, LFO rate, LFO pitch, Reverb SP-404MKII 1–4 = BUS 1–4, 5 = INPUT FX Ctrl 1–4, FX on, FX select S-1 its channel Cutoff, Reso, Filter env, Decay, Delay, Reverb

Each names every CC in the synth's MIDI chart. They are in midi_presets/ in the source; more synths are welcome.

docs.title: The preset file
docs.text:
Presets are text files in MidiPresets/ on the card, named <name>.txt, so they can be written or edited on a computer. For example, a Roland S-1:

# OpenTracker MIDI preset
velocity = 127
offset = 0
slot A = 74
slot B = 71
slot C = 24
slot D = 75
slot E = 92
slot F = 91
cc 3 = LFO Rate
cc 24 = Filt Env
cc 71 = Reso
cc 74 = Cutoff
cc 75 = Decay
cc 91 = Reverb
cc 92 = Delay
lfo target = slot A
lfo depth = 30
  • slot A … slot F: a CC number (0–127), PC (program change), AT (channel pressure) or PAT (poly aftertouch).
  • cc n = name: the name of CC n (0–127), up to 9 characters.
  • lfo target: off, slot A … slot F, PB (pitch bend) or AT. CC n also works: it picks the slot set to CC n.
  • lfo shape: 0 Rev saw, 1 Saw, 2 Triangle, 3 Square, 4 Random.
  • lfo rate: 0 (128 steps per cycle) to 22 (1/8 step), as listed on the LFO page.
  • lfo depth 0–64 (the swing either side of the center), lfo center 0–127, lfo retrigger 0 Free or 1 Note.

Lines starting with # are comments, keys ignore case, and a missing or unknown line keeps the default, so a preset can be as short as one cc line.

docs.title: Note names
docs.text: Config > General > Note names: Sharps / Flats / Auto. Auto spells notes the way the project's scale does, modes included: C Mixolydian shows B♭, not A♯. Display only.

docs.title: Piano pads
docs.text:
Config > General > Pad layout: Stock / Piano. Piano turns the pads into two keyboards that light up as ones, laid out as on grid controllers: each pair of rows is a keyboard, with the white keys along the lower row and the black keys in the row above, each black key over the white key to its right.

·  C# D# ·  F# G# A# ·  C# D# ·  F#     upper keyboard
C  D  E  F  G  A  B  C  D  E  F  G
·  C# D# ·  F# G# A# ·  C# D# ·  F#     lower keyboard
C  D  E  F  G  A  B  C  D  E  F  G
  • Each keyboard spans an octave and a fifth; the upper one is the same keyboard an octave higher.
  • The pads marked · (over C and F, where a piano has no black key) are dark and play nothing.
  • The bottom-left C is the C of the project's root note octave. To play higher or lower, change the root note.
  • The lights show the keyboard. With a scale picked, the scale's keys light at one level, black or white, the root brighter; keys outside the scale stay playable but are barely lit, so the scale shows on the keyboard. In Chromatic the lights draw a piano: white keys lit, black keys a little dimmer, the root brightest.
  • It works wherever the pads play notes: the pattern editor's Note column, Sample Playback, the instrument pages, the synth browser, the Sample Editor and the recorder. In the pattern editor the step's note (and, with Pads preview, the notes on the current line) lights at full brightness.
  • Pads that do something else keep their own lights: the Instr and FX columns, Performance, the synth edit page, and Beat Slice instruments (one pad per slice).
  • Stock is the default and keeps the original layout. The setting is global, not saved with the project.

docs.title: Chord hints
docs.text:
With a scale picked (Config > Project Settings), hold a key on the piano pads and the notes of its chord light up. In A minor, hold E: on the upper keyboard E, G and B light (Em, the chord on E in the key), on the lower keyboard E, G# and B (E major, its alternate). Press the lit keys to play the chord. The screen shows Em v: E G B / E V: E G# B while you hold it.

  • The upper keyboard shows the chord built from the scale's own notes (every other note of the scale: root, 3rd, 5th), with its number in the key (v).
  • The lower keyboard shows the alternate major / minor chord on the same root: the 3rd moved a semitone, so a minor chord becomes major and the other way round. Some of these are common outside notes (E major in A minor is the V chord of harmonic minor), others just a colour to try. Diminished and augmented chords have none.
  • With Note names on Auto the notes are spelled from the key, one letter per note of the scale: in F# major the chord on E# is E#dim: E# G# B, not F. With Sharps or Flats they follow that setting.
  • In a mode the hints show the mode's own chords (in D Dorian, G is major: G IV). Song mode progressions play modes as their parallel major or minor key, so a chord from a progression can differ from the hint (i VI in D Dorian is Dm Bb).
  • No hints in Chromatic or in scales of fewer than 5 notes, or where the pads do something else (Performance).

docs.title: Chord entry
docs.text:
In the pattern editor's edit mode (stopped), pads pressed while another note pad is still held make a chord: the first note goes on the cursor's step and the cursor moves on as usual; each further note goes on the same step, one track to the right. Hold the chord's pads together, release them, and play the next chord.

  • With a selection over several tracks, the chord fills the selected tracks on the selection's first step instead, and the cursor stays.
  • One Undo removes the whole chord.
  • A track that can't play the current instrument (a MIDI track for a sample instrument) ends the chord there.
  • Live recording (Rec while playing) already spreads a chord over the next free tracks.

docs.title: Slices to pattern
docs.text:
Chop a break, then press one key to get a pattern that plays it. Without this you would enter every slice by hand on the right step before the break even plays straight; with it, flipping the break is plain pattern editing.

For example, with a 2-bar drum break:

  1. Load it into an instrument. On Sample Playback, pick Slice mode and press F1 Auto: it cuts at each hit, say into 12 slices.
  2. Open the More page (F6). F4 Steps shows 32 (2 bars at the song tempo); turn the encoder if it guessed wrong.
  3. With the pattern cursor on an empty track, press F5 To Pattern. The track gets one note per slice, on the step where its hit is: slice 1 as C2, slice 2 as C#2, and so on.
step  1    2    3    4    5    6    7  …
note  C2   ---  C#2  ---  D2   ---  D#2
      kick      hat       snare     hat
  1. Press Play: the break plays as recorded, in time. Now edit the track as any other: change a note to swap a hit (slice 3 → slice 1 puts a kick where the snare was), delete notes for space, or repeat the snare slice for a roll.

On the Sample Playback screen (Slice or Beat Slice mode), the More page (F6) has:

Key Does Steps (F4) How many steps the sample lasts. The guess is its length at the song tempo, rounded to 1, 2, 4 or 8 bars; turn the encoder if it guessed wrong (a 2-bar break at 92 BPM in a 140 BPM song reads as 4 bars). To Pattern (F5) Writes the slices on the pattern's current track (the one the cursor was on).
  • Slice i goes on the step nearest where it starts, as note 24 + i, with the steps in between empty, so each slice plays on to the next one. The trigs repeat every Steps steps to the end of the track.
  • The track is cleared first; it asks when the track had steps. Undo in the pattern editor brings them back.
  • A Slice instrument turns Beat Slice, so each note plays its own slice.
  • At another song tempo the slices play at their own speed and pitch (as REX loops do): a faster song cuts each slice short at the next trig, a slower one leaves a short gap after it. The pattern keeps its length; a sample longer than the track is placed once, cut at the track's end.
  • Slice first: Auto (F1) for drum breaks, Evenly (F2) for loops in time.

docs.title: Instrument library
docs.text:
Keep a sample instrument you've set up (its sample, play mode, slices, envelopes, filter, effects…) and use it again in any project. On the Instrument Effects page (Instrument Params, then More):

  • Save (F7) opens the keyboard with the instrument's name; Save writes it to Instruments/<name>.pti on the card (into the folder you last opened in Load). An existing name asks before replacing it.
  • Load (F6) lists Instruments/: folders first, then instruments. F8 opens a folder or loads the instrument into the current slot (replacing it); Left goes up a folder (at Instruments/ it closes the list); F7 cancels. Folders can be nested as deep as you like.

  • The files are stock .pti instruments: the Sample Loader lists them too, and stock firmware loads them.
  • A long instrument streamed from the card is copied in full first, so Save can take a moment.
  • An instrument that doesn't fit in the free sample memory isn't loaded ("Not enough sample memory"); the slot keeps what it had.
  • A multisample instrument saves as a Slice instrument (one zone per slice, as stock firmware sees it): the zones' root notes and the Multi play mode are kept with the project, not in the .pti.

docs.title: Memory
docs.text:
Config > Memory shows what fills the Tracker's memory, for when something won't load. For example, with DX7 on a synth slot, turning on the last card effects can fail with "Card memory full". The page shows DX7 taking 18 KB of the card memory, so you know to turn off an effect or switch the slot to a built-in synth.

  • Card modules: the card synths and effects that are loaded (DX7, Echo …), what uses them (synth, slot 2, synth, P3 for a synth preset, effect) and their size. Ones that are wanted but not in are listed too, with why: loads at Stop, no room (red), didn't load.
  • Sample memory: the samples, plus what is borrowed from it: card effects' buffers (Echo's 48 KB line) and the space held back while resampling or during a tape stop.
  • The bar turns red at 90 %. The page is read-only.

When a card module doesn't fit, the notice names the biggest one loaded, e.g. "Echo: Card memory full (DX7 18.3 KB)", and the FX bank shows how much card memory is used. In the simulator the card modules are built in, so the page lists only the sample memory.

docs.title: Colour themes
docs.text:
Make a theme in Tracker CE's theme editor, press Export Theme, and copy the .json file to the Themes folder on the card. Pick it under Config > General > Display theme, after the three built-in themes. Themes made for Tracker CE work on OpenTracker, and the other way round.

  • Export theme (Config > General) saves the theme you're using, built-in or not, as Themes/<name>.json. Import that into the editor to start from it. An existing file is never overwritten.
  • A theme draws in CE's style: flat panels without fades, and the band across the pattern only on the playing row while the song plays. The built-in themes keep the stock look.
  • Colours a file leaves out come from its base (Original, Monochrome or Anniversary). Keys that have no counterpart on OpenTracker (CE's mini menu and on-screen keyboard) are ignored, and they aren't written on export.
  • Text set to its own background colour (unreadable) falls back to the base's colours.
  • Twelve example themes are in themes/ in the repository, among them Halloween (contributed by AnthonyBerg1983).
  • The old key = value text themes (.txt) are no longer read.

docs.title: The 2.x features (from upstream)
docs.text: The 2.x line brings the newer Tracker features to the original hardware. In short:

docs.title: Tracker Mini project compatibility
docs.text:
• Projects are saved in the Tracker 2.2.1 format: 16-track patterns, the three synth slots, track names and mutes for tracks 13–16.
  • Synth patches use the Mini's .patch files, stored with the project and in a library at Patches/<ENGINE>/. All 299 Mini factory patches load and save back unchanged.

docs.title: 16 tracks
docs.text:
• Tracks 13–16 work like MIDI tracks 9–12: notes, MIDI channels, CC A–F, pitch bend, velocity, mute and solo. Performance Play mode, Pattern length and Step repeater act on them too.
  • Pattern pages through all 16 tracks; Song shows a scrolling 12-track window. Fill, copy and paste work across all 16.

docs.title: Synth engines (instruments S1–S3)
docs.text:
• Three synth slots, played from any track as instruments S1–S3.
  • Engines: ACD (acid bass and lead, 24 dB and ladder-style filters, glide), VAP (virtual-analog poly, morphing oscillators, hard sync, 15 filter types, a 6-slot modulation matrix), PERC (a drum kit), FAT (unison supersaw), WTFM (two-operator wavetable FM), and in this fork DX7 (from the card).
  • Macros: FX columns A–F drive macros 1–6, and Volume drives macro 7.
  • Voices: a shared pool of 4 by default, adjustable in Config > General > Synth voices (1–8). If the audio gets close to its limit, only synth voices are cut; sample tracks never are.
  • Screens after the Mini's layout: Synth Parameters, Synth Macros, the Load Patch popup with Preview, and the synth level columns on Global Mixer page 3. In this fork Edit Patch is laid out like Config, with a help box.
  • Exports include separate stems synth_1..3.wav.

docs.title: Export sample rate
docs.text: Config > General > Export sample rate: 44.1 kHz (default) or 44117 Hz. The Tracker's audio runs at 44,117 Hz. At 44.1 kHz, exported songs, patterns, stems and renders are converted to a standard 44,100 Hz WAV, so they play in time in any DAW. 44117 Hz writes the Tracker's own rate, as the original firmware does.

docs.title: Radio stereo
docs.text: Config > General > Radio stereo: Off (default) or On. On records the built-in radio in stereo, and the Sample Recorder's source list shows Radio ST. Off keeps it mono, as the original firmware does: mono is cleaner on weak stations and doubles the recording time.

docs.title: Stereo samples
docs.text: Stereo WAVs keep both channels and play in stereo in one-shot, loop, slice and beat-slice modes; pan works as balance.

docs.title: CPU meter
docs.text: Config > General > CPU meter: Auto, Always or Off shows the audio load in the title bar.

docs.title: USB Storage mode
docs.text:
Config > USB > USB Storage: On shows the SD card on a connected computer as a USB drive, as on the Tracker Mini, so projects, samples and patches can be copied without taking the card out.

  • Playback stops and the project is saved first. Keep the power and the cable connected while files are copied.
  • To finish, eject the drive on the computer, then press Exit (or set the row back to Off). The project reloads from the card.
  • It's always Off after power-on. About 1 MB/s (full-speed USB). USB MIDI and the serial log keep working.
  • On Windows the Tracker may appear once as a new device (new COM/MIDI port).

docs.title: Multisample instruments
docs.text:
A multisample instrument holds several recordings of one sound, one per note (a Juno pad sampled every few semitones, say). Each key plays the nearest recording, repitched by the distance, so the sound stays natural across the keyboard instead of stretching one sample over five octaves.

The Tracker loads them from SFZ files, a plain-text format most sample packs and samplers use.

docs.title: Get an SFZ
docs.text:
Many packs ship one: copy the pack folder (WAVs and .sfz together) to the card.

For a folder of note samples without an SFZ, tools/make_sfz.py writes one on the computer, from the file names:

tools/make_sfz.py ~/Samples/MyPack

It looks into every subfolder, reads the note from a leading MIDI number (054 Dusty Pluck Junos F#2.wav) or a note name (Pad C3.wav), and skips folders with fewer than 8 notes (kits, chords). --name-octave 3 is for packs that call middle C "C3"; --dry-run shows what it would write. Then copy the folders to the card.

docs.title: Load it
docs.text:
1. In the Sample Loader, pick an empty instrument on the right. To hear a pack first, hold F3 Preview on its .sfz: it plays the pack's sample nearest middle C (C4), as a WAV previews. Up / Down while holding it previews the next file.
  2. Select the .sfz file and press Add. A panel opens instead of loading at once:
Key Sets F1 Low / F2 High the note range to load F3 Every the spacing: every note, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 6th or 12th F4 Max length cuts each note to 8 s ... 0.5 s with a short fade (Full keeps them whole) Size what it takes in sample memory (shown only) F6 Cancel / F8 Load

Turn the encoder to change the selected value. The panel says how many notes the SFZ has, which ones it will load and how much memory is left. It opens with values that fit in about half the free memory, so another instrument still fits; Load is greyed while the choice doesn't fit or no note is in the range.

At most 48 notes go into one instrument: space them out or narrow the range for a bigger pack. A spacing of a 3rd or 4th note usually sounds as good as every note.

docs.title: Play it
docs.text:
The instrument plays like any other: pads, the pattern, MIDI in. Its Sample Playback page shows the ninth play mode, Multi:

  • Zone (F1) steps through the loaded notes and Root shows each one's note; F5 zooms. The zone edges stay where the loader put them.
  • Switching to another play mode keeps the notes: switch back to Multi any time.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Multisamples load mono, as one-shots: SFZ loops, velocity layers and round robins aren't used yet. Each note plays to its end (or its Max length).
  • The notes are saved in the project like any sample. Stock firmware and the Tracker Mini open the project too and play the instrument as a Slice instrument, one slice per note.
  • Long samples take a lot of memory: a 10 s mono note is about 0.9 MB. Max length is the quickest way to fit a pack.

docs.title: Performance mode
docs.text: The Performance screen plays effects live from the pads: 12 columns, each an effect type, with 3 stored values per column on the pad rows. The fork adds scenes with a crossfader, a bank of 16 scenes, master FX (DJ filter, tape stop), MIDI CC columns that play an external synth's parameters and Master FX columns that play the master effects (Echo, Chorus, Dirt ...).

docs.title: Basics (as in stock)
docs.text:
• Press Performance. Hold a pad to play that column's value on its row; release to go back. The top row shows what's playing.
  • Rec (edit mode): the encoder changes the value of the selected row. In the fork, a tapped row can be edited with the encoder without holding the pad.
  • Choosing a column's effect type (fork): in edit mode, Up / Down open a list of every type on the column's current one, on the left of the screen (the title names the column). Move with the encoder (Shift + a quick turn for bigger jumps) or Up / Down, then press OK (F8). Cancel (F7), Left / Right or Rec close it without changing anything (for MIDI CC and Master FX, Left / Right move between their lists instead). Nothing is applied until OK, and the F keys don't switch track effects while the list is open. The row values stay when the new type has the same range (e.g. Volume to Panning); otherwise they're cleared as in stock. Stock stepped the type with Up / Down, applying each one on the way.

- The F keys turn the effects on or off per track (on = red label). Every track starts off, as in stock, so tap the F keys of the tracks the pads should reach. Shift + F key mutes the track. Left / Right (outside edit mode) switch the F keys between tracks 1–8 and 9–16. In the fork the F keys are remembered: leaving the screen and coming back keeps them, and they're saved with the project (stock turns every track off again).

  • Effect types include Volume, Panning, Tune, Low-pass / High-pass / Band-pass, Delay and Reverb send, Start / End pos, Direction, the LFOs, Repeater, Play mode, Length, Bit depth and Overdrive, plus the fork's DJ filter, Tape stop, MIDI CC and Master FX.

docs.title: Scenes and the crossfader
docs.text:
A scene stores a row for every column. The crossfader's two ends, A and B, each play a scene; the encoder (outside edit mode) or MIDI CC 63 fades between them.

  • Continuous values (volume, filters, sends …) fade smoothly. Filters cross over at the middle (a low-pass on A and a high-pass on B don't fight). Stepped effects (Repeater, Direction, Tape stop …) switch at the middle. With fader ranges, each column can move over its own part of the fader instead.
  • The title bar shows the pair (A 1 |------| B 2) and where the fader is. Rows of the scene on A are marked red, on B blue; the pad LEDs and the green (active) row follow the fader.
  • A pad pressed on a column the scenes drive takes it over: its row plays and turns green. The next fader move hands the column back to the scenes.

docs.title: Store and clear while playing
docs.text: Keys Does Shift + Left / Right Store the current pad rows into the scene on A / B. Delete + Left / Right Clear the scene on A / B. Hold pads + Shift / Delete + Left / Right Store / clear only the held columns.

docs.title: Which tracks get the effects
docs.text:
Storing a whole scene (Shift + Left / Right with no pad held) also stores which tracks have their effects on (the F keys). When that scene is loaded again, the F keys follow it:

  • putting it on A or B (from the bank page or a song slot),
  • moving the fader past the middle, to the scene on the other side.

So a song can have the drums in the Repeater in the verse and everything in the chorus. A scene stored before (or cleared with Delete) carries no F keys and leaves them as they are. Tapping an F key while a scene plays works as usual; the scene's setting comes back the next time the scene is loaded or the fader crosses the middle. Storing only some columns (pads held) doesn't change a scene's F keys.
