docs.title: VAP
docs.text:
A two-oscillator virtual analog polysynth after the Tracker Mini's VAP: oscillators that morph from triangle to saw to pulse, a 15-type filter, three envelopes, two LFOs and a modulation matrix.

VAP's sound engine is our own design, built to the Tracker Mini's VAP settings.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Two oscillators. Shape morphs each one from a triangle (0) through a saw (50) to a pulse (100); PW sets the pulse's width. Mix balances the two, and Envelope 2 can move the balance over the note (Mix Env Amt). Tune sets each oscillator in semitones; Detune spreads the two apart and Finetune moves both. Sync restarts oscillator 2 with oscillator 1, and Noise adds white noise.

Filter: 15 types (low-pass, high-pass, band-pass and notch, in several flavours and slopes) with Envelope 1 on the cutoff (Env Amt) and Note Track.

Envelopes: the Amp Env shapes the volume, Envelope 1 the filter, and Envelope 2 the oscillator Mix; all three can also be sent in the Modulation section.

LFOs: two, each with a waveform, a rate (or a note length with Sync On) and a Retrigger mode. They do nothing until a Modulation slot sends them somewhere.

Modulation: six slots, each sending a source (an envelope or an LFO) to a destination (pulse width, Mix, Shape, pitch, cutoff, a sustain level, volume, noise or Envelope 1's decay) by an amount, plus or minus.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: What each setting does, as the Edit Patch help box shows it.

docs.title: Oscillators
docs.text: The two oscillators, their mix, tuning, sync and noise.

docs.title: Mix
docs.text:
The balance between oscillator 1 and oscillator 2.

  • 0 % is both equally; minus is more oscillator 1, plus more 2.

docs.title: Shape 1
docs.text:
Oscillator 1's waveform: triangle, saw or pulse, and in between.

  • 0 is a triangle, 50 a saw, 100 a pulse.

docs.title: Shape 2
docs.text:
Oscillator 2's waveform: triangle, saw or pulse, and in between.

  • 0 is a triangle, 50 a saw, 100 a pulse.

docs.title: PW 1
docs.text:
Oscillator 1's pulse width, when Shape 1 is towards a pulse.

  • 0 is a square; minus or plus makes the pulse narrower.

docs.title: PW 2
docs.text:
Oscillator 2's pulse width, when Shape 2 is towards a pulse.

  • 0 is a square; minus or plus makes the pulse narrower.

docs.title: Tune 1
docs.text:
Oscillator 1's tuning in semitones.

  • 0 is the note; +7 is a 5th up, +12 an octave.

docs.title: Tune 2
docs.text:
Oscillator 2's tuning in semitones.

  • 0 is the note; +7 is a 5th up, +12 an octave.

docs.title: Finetune
docs.text:
Fine-tunes both oscillators, in cents.

  • 0 is in tune; 100 cents is a semitone.

docs.title: Detune
docs.text:
Spreads the two oscillators apart, one down and one up.

  • 0 keeps them together; 100 cents puts them a semitone apart.

docs.title: Noise
docs.text:
White noise mixed into the oscillators.

  • 0 % is off.

docs.title: Sync
docs.text:
Hard sync: oscillator 2 restarts with oscillator 1.

  • Off: the oscillators run free.
  • On: oscillator 2 restarts each cycle of oscillator 1; tune it to change the tone.

docs.title: Reset 1
docs.text:
Whether oscillator 1 restarts at each note.

  • Off: runs free, so each note starts at a different point.
  • On: restarts at each note: every note starts the same.

docs.title: Reset 2
docs.text:
Whether oscillator 2 restarts at each note.

  • Off: runs free, so each note starts at a different point.
  • On: restarts at each note: every note starts the same.

docs.title: Mix Env Amt
docs.text:
How much Envelope 2 moves Mix over the note; minus moves it the other way.

  • 0 % is off.

docs.title: Filter
docs.text: The filter after the oscillators, with Envelope 1 on its cutoff.

docs.title: Cutoff
docs.text:
Where the filter cuts.

  • Low is dark and muffled; high lets everything through.

docs.title: Resonance
docs.text:
How much the filter rings at the cutoff.

  • 0 % is smooth; high values ring strongly at the cutoff.

docs.title: Type
docs.text:
The filter type.

  • LP MG 24dB: low-pass, MG flavour with a driven input, 24 dB: cuts the highs steeply.
  • LP OB 24dB: low-pass, OB flavour with soft clipping, 24 dB.
  • LP OB 12dB: low-pass, OB flavour with soft clipping, 12 dB: gentler.
  • LP SVF 24dB: low-pass, clean state-variable, 24 dB.
  • LP SVF 12dB: low-pass, clean state-variable, 12 dB: gentler.
  • HP OB 24dB: high-pass, OB flavour, 24 dB: cuts the lows steeply.
  • HP OB 12dB: high-pass, OB flavour, 12 dB: gentler.
  • HP SVF 24dB: high-pass, clean state-variable, 24 dB.
  • HP SVF 12dB: high-pass, clean state-variable, 12 dB: gentler.
  • BP OB 24dB: band-pass, OB flavour, 24 dB: keeps a narrow band.
  • BP OB 12dB: band-pass, OB flavour, 12 dB: a wider band.
  • BP SVF 24dB: band-pass, clean state-variable, 24 dB: a narrow band.
  • BP SVF 12dB: band-pass, clean state-variable, 12 dB: a wider band.
  • Notch SVF 24dB: notch: cuts a band around the cutoff, 24 dB.
  • Notch SVF 12dB: notch: cuts a band around the cutoff, 12 dB.

docs.title: Env Amt
docs.text:
How much Envelope 1 moves the cutoff; minus moves it down.

  • 0 % leaves the cutoff still; 100 % sweeps up to 10 octaves.

docs.title: Note Track
docs.text:

  • 100 % moves the cutoff an octave per octave; 0 % keeps it fixed.

docs.title: Amp Env

docs.title: Attack

docs.title: Decay

docs.title: Sustain

  • 0 % dies away after Decay; 100 % stays at full volume.

docs.title: Release
docs.text:

  • 0 stops at once; higher values leave a tail.

docs.title: Ratio

docs.title: Waveform
docs.text:
The LFO's shape.

  • Triangle: straight lines up and down.
  • Sine: smooth up and down.
  • Ramp Up: rises, then drops at once.
  • Ramp Down: drops, then jumps back up.
  • Square: jumps between two values.
  • Random S&H: a new random value each cycle.

docs.title: Retrigger
docs.text:

  • Free Running: runs on, shared by all the slot's voices.
  • One Shot: starts at each note and runs one cycle.
  • Note: starts again at each note, then keeps going.

docs.title: Sync
docs.text:

docs.title: Modulation
docs.text: Six slots, each sending a source to a destination by an amount.

docs.title: Src 1
docs.text:
What slot 1 sends.

  • Amp Env: the volume envelope.
  • Env 1 (Fltr): Envelope 1, the filter envelope.
  • Env 2: Envelope 2.
  • LFO 1: LFO 1.
  • LFO 2: LFO 2.

docs.title: Dest 1
docs.text:
What slot 1 moves.

  • Osc1 PWM: oscillator 1's pulse width.
  • Osc2 PWM: oscillator 2's pulse width.
  • Osc Mix: the oscillator Mix.
  • Filter Cutoff: the filter's cutoff.
  • Amp Env Sustain: the Amp Env's Sustain level.
  • Flt Env Sustain: Envelope 1's Sustain level.
  • Wave Env Sustain: Envelope 2's Sustain level.
  • Volume: the volume.
  • Osc1 Pitch: oscillator 1's pitch.
  • Osc2 Pitch: oscillator 2's pitch.
  • Flt Env Decay: Envelope 1's Decay time.
  • Noise Volume: the noise level.
  • Osc1 Shape: Shape 1.
  • Osc2 Shape: Shape 2.

docs.title: Amt 1
docs.text:
How much slot 1 moves its destination; minus moves it the other way.

  • 0 % is off; on a pitch, 100 % is up to 4 octaves.

docs.title: Src 2
docs.text:
What slot 2 sends.

  • Amp Env: the volume envelope.
  • Env 1 (Fltr): Envelope 1, the filter envelope.
  • Env 2: Envelope 2.

docs.title: WTFM
docs.text:
A two-operator FM synth with shapeable operators, after the Tracker Mini's WTFM: each operator plays a waveform row you can morph, operator 2 modulates operator 1, and a filter, three envelopes, two LFOs and a modulation matrix follow.

WTFM's sound engine is our own design, built to the Tracker Mini's WTFM settings.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Two operators. Operator 1 is what you hear; operator 2 modulates it (FM). Each plays a Character row, and Shape moves along the row:

  • Smoother, Sharper and Wilder morph towards a saw and on to a square as Shape goes up. Smoother starts from a sine, Sharper from a triangle; Wilder is Sharper folded for extra overtones.
  • Add 1 to Add 11 start as a sine and add a series of overtones (every harmonic for Add 1, every 2nd for Add 2, and so on); Shape sets how much.

Each operator's pitch is the note times its Ratio (0.25 to 12), plus Finetune. Feedback 1 and Feedback 2 make each operator modulate itself; Feedback 2>1 feeds operator 2 into operator 1's feedback. Reset restarts an operator at the start of each note; Off lets it run free. Oversampling runs operator 1 at twice the sample rate, which reduces aliasing at high FM and Feedback, at more CPU.

Filter: 15 types (low-pass, high-pass, band-pass and notch, in several flavours and slopes) with Envelope 1 on the cutoff (Env Amt) and Note Track.

Envelopes: the Amp Env shapes the volume, Envelope 1 the filter, and Envelope 2 has no fixed job: send it anywhere in the Modulation section.

LFOs: two, each with a waveform, a rate (or a note length with Sync On) and a Retrigger mode.

Modulation: six slots, each sending a source (an envelope or an LFO) to a destination (pitch, Shape, Feedback, FM, cutoff, a sustain level, volume or Envelope 1's decay) by an amount, plus or minus.
